text:
B: Hiya, sorry, erm, can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. Hiya. Joanne.
B: I'm Holly. I'm in Stockport. Sorry, I always ask that, I'm convinced my laptop's gonna die.
A: It's fine. Mine's ancient. I'm in St Helens.
B: Oh, we're not far, then. Like, forty minutes?
A: Something like that. I don't go to Manchester much. Too busy.
B: It is busy. I get the train every day for work and it's late, like, constantly. Erm, what do you do? Sorry, I've asked everyone that.
A: I look after me mum. She's got dementia. So I'm not working.
B: Oh, I'm sorry. That's, erm, that's really hard, I think. My nan's getting a bit forgetful, but not like, properly.
A: It starts like that. Forgetting names, putting things in the wrong place. Me mum put her keys in the fridge once and we were looking for an hour.
B: Aw, no.
A: We laugh about it now. Some days you can't, mind.
B: Yeah. My mum's a physio at the hospital, and she says the families have the hardest time, like, more than people think. Sorry, I don't know if that helps.
A: No, it's true. Everyone asks about her. Nobody asks how you're doing. Is your mum NHS, then?
B: Yeah, Stepping Hill. She's always knackered.
A: I bet. I'm on the phone to the surgery every other day. Ringing at eight, on hold forty minutes, then they've got no appointments. I'm not rude, but I tell them straight.
B: I couldn't do that. I get anxious ringing for a takeaway, haha.
A: You get used to it when you have to. What do you do, then?
B: I'm an apprentice in a lab. Quality control. So I test samples and log everything. I'm alright at the testing, I'm just a bit disorganised with the paperwork side.
A: Is that like a proper science job, then?
B: Yeah, kind of. I want to do a degree apprenticeship after, so I don't have uni debt.
A: That's sensible. I didn't think you'd be that sensible, to be honest. From the photo.
B: Haha, oh no, was it the messy room?
A: A bit. Mine's not much better. The cat sicked up on the settee this morning.
B: Oh no! What's her name?
A: Mabel. Tabby. She's about fifteen. Eats the grass in the yard then brings it back up inside.
B: My dog does that! Bonnie. She eats it in the park and then she's sick in the hall. My mum goes mad.
A: They're not daft, are they. Never on the lino.
B: Never on the lino, haha. Erm, do you get any time off, like, for yourself?
A: Walk round the park mornings. And I read. Thrillers, from the library. I guessed the end of the last one by page fifty.
B: Oh, I'd never guess. I just cry at everything.
A: You'd not like the ones I read, then.
B: Probably not, no. Is it like murders and...
